subject: ss-paediatric-cardiology
title: Cardiomyopathies, myocarditis and pericardial disease in children
refs: American Heart Association pediatric heart failure guidance

steps.tx: **Dilated cardiomyopathy** dilates and weakens the left ventricle, presenting in infants with tachypnoea, poor feeding and hepatomegaly. Echocardiogram shows enlarged chambers with low shortening fraction below 28 percent. Heart failure therapy with digoxin, diuretics and afterload reduction stabilises symptoms before transplant evaluation.
steps.say: Dilated cardiomyopathy dilates and weakens the left ventricle, presenting in infants with tachypnoea, poor feeding and hepatomegaly. Echocardiogram shows enlarged chambers with low shortening fraction. Heart failure therapy with diuretics and afterload reduction stabilises symptoms before transplant evaluation.

steps.tx: **Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy** thickens septum and narrows outflow, causing effort syncope and sudden death in adolescents during exertion. Echocardiogram classifies concentric versus asymmetric hypertrophy with left ventricular outflow gradient at rest and stress. Beta blockers protect against dynamic obstruction, while septal reduction suits refractory gradient with drug failure.
steps.say: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy thickens the septum and narrows outflow, causing effort syncope and sudden death in adolescents. Echocardiogram classifies hypertrophy with outflow gradient. Beta blockers protect against dynamic obstruction, while septal reduction suits refractory gradient.

steps.tx: **Restrictive cardiomyopathy** stiffens myocardium so diastolic filling fails despite normal contractility and preserved ejection in children. Dip and plateau waveforms on catheterisation expose restrictive physiology with raised pressures. Prognosis remains poor, and transplantation is the only curative option for progressive disease awaiting donors.

steps.tx: **Myocarditis** inflames myocardium after viral illness, presenting as chest pain, arrhythmia or heart failure in young children. Troponin rises with cardiac magnetic resonance showing oedema and late enhancement in the injured wall. Supportive care with activity restriction and heart failure therapy covers most cases without immunosuppression routinely.
steps.say: Myocarditis inflames the myocardium after viral illness, presenting as chest pain, arrhythmia or heart failure. Troponin rises with cardiac magnetic resonance showing oedema and late enhancement. Supportive care with activity restriction and heart failure therapy covers most cases.

steps.tx: **Viral aetiology** behind myocarditis includes coxsackievirus, adenovirus and parvovirus B19 in seasonal clusters across childhood. Endomyocardial biopsy remains gold standard but rarely performed in children due to risk and sampling limits. Most epidemics resolve with supportive care, though giant cell variants need aggressive therapy and transplant listing.

steps.tx: **Pericarditis** in children shows pleuritic pain relieved by sitting forward with pericardial friction rub and breathlessness. Electrocardiogram with widespread concave elevation and low voltage confirms inflammation across the heart surface. High dose aspirin or ibuprofen plus colchicine hastens resolution and prevents recurrence in most cases.
steps.say: Pericarditis in children shows pleuritic pain relieved by sitting forward with a pericardial friction rub. Electrocardiogram with widespread concave elevation confirms inflammation. High dose aspirin or ibuprofen plus colchicine hastens resolution and prevents recurrence.

steps.tx: **Constrictive pericarditis** thickens pericardium and impairs diastolic filling with raised venous pressures causing hepatomegaly. Pericardial calcification on computed tomography supports constriction over restriction with thickened layers. Pericardiectomy removes the rigid shell and restores diastolic expansion with sustained relief after surgery.
steps.say: Constrictive pericarditis thickens the pericardium and impairs diastolic filling with raised venous pressures. Pericardial calcification on computed tomography supports constriction over restriction. Pericardiectomy removes the rigid shell and restores diastolic expansion.

steps.tx: **Pericardial tamponade** compresses chambers when effusion raises intrapericardial pressure above diastolic filling pressure distorting cardiac output. Beck triad with hypotension, muffled sounds and raised neck veins signals tamponade in older children urgently. Emergency pericardiocentesis relieves tamponade and restores filling within minutes with monitoring.

steps.tx: **Prognosis** of dilated disease improves with early failure therapy, while hypertrophic sudden death risk needs family screening and sports restriction. Myocarditis recurrence falls with activity restriction for six months after onset. Constrictive disease cures with pericardiectomy, whereas restrictive disease progresses to transplantation.

steps.tx: **Final table** anchors echo cutoffs, drug choices and gold standard tests: shortening below 28 percent defines dilated disease, beta blockers protect hypertrophic outflow, colchicine prevents pericarditis recurrence, and pericardiocentesis treats tamponade. Biopsy confirms myocarditis, calcification confirms constriction, and failure therapy bridges toward transplantation.
